FOMC — hike vs hold; Bianco sees 7-5 split

posts.text: The surprise summer global bull market continues.
FOMC vote on September 16th will be 7-5. Not sure if it is 7-5 to hike or 7-5 to hold. Warsh is 1 of 12 votes. Jackson Hole only moved hike odds to 58%, not 85%+.
Warsh: hard pressed to describe broad financial conditions as restrictive. Summer PCE/CPI better than expected but underlying trends have not meaningfully improved. Otherwise we have work to do.
Options market post Warsh: lean into bullish/call stance in bonds and equities has faded toward put skew. Reads more disappointment vs fear.
Lots of positive gamma support today for SPX and aggregate single stocks. Dealers should buy dips.
Institutional investors extremely bullish. Asset-manager long S&P 500 futures ~$375B, near record. +$160B / +74% since April 2025.
Bullish positioning in gold surging. GLD call minus put OI ~2.4 million, highest since February. Macro and currency uncertainty.
JPMorgan flagged growing risks of a late-summer or early-autumn market downturn despite major indexes remaining in bullish trends.
After Cruel Summer for bonds, Citadel Securities macro maven flips bullish on duration.
Spain CPI (Y/Y) Aug P: 4.3% (est 4.2%; prev 3.6%) — hotter European inflation.
France Aug CPI y/y 2.4% vs 2.1% prior; harmonized slightly hot.
Rates first, stocks second. Friday NFP moves September hike odds more than any earnings print. VIX still near year lows.
S&P roughly 1.1% off the Aug 13 high. Big-cap tech held; small caps did not. Volume light, VIX near year lows.
Warsh Jackson Hole: underlying trends have not meaningfully improved. Bond market heard hike risk — Sep 15-16 odds ~55-60%.
